title: 5d-4: boundary resolver
description:
## Parent

sutra/68 — 5d PRD: constraint system + DD integration

## What to build

New `resolver.rs` module in `src/constraints/`. Resolves component-level boundary constraints to file-level `(file_id, file_id)` forbidden pairs by joining against the `component_membership` table. File-level `forbidden_dep` constraints pass through directly. Output feeds into the DD engine's `SetForbiddenPairs` command.

Caches resolved pairs tagged with a generation counter on component_membership. Re-resolves when generation bumps (component recompute or constraint file change). This keeps DD simple — it only sees file IDs.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Resolver module with component_membership join
- [ ] Feeds resolved pairs into DD
- [ ] Generation-counter caching
- [ ] Cache invalidation on membership change
- [ ] Pass-through for file-level forbidden_deps
- [ ] Tests for resolution, caching, invalidation

## Blocked by

- sutra/70 — 5d-2: constraint types + rules parsing
- sutra/71 — 5d-3: DD forbidden pairs maintained view

acceptance_criteria.text: New resolver module (src/constraints/resolver.rs) that joins boundary constraints against component_membership to produce file-level forbidden pairs
Resolved pairs feed into DD via SetForbiddenPairs
Resolution cached with generation counter on component_membership
Cache invalidated and re-resolved when component membership changes
Cache hit (no re-resolution) when membership unchanged
file-level forbidden_dep constraints pass through resolver without component_membership join
Tests cover: boundary constraint resolution with mock membership, cache hit/miss, membership change triggers re-resolution, mixed boundary + forbidden_dep constraints

messages.author: codex
messages.text:
Codex review: needs-attention. 2 high findings on resolver cache.

1. [high] Cache ignores constraints and path_map inputs — only keyed by clustering_meta. A rules-only change or path_map change returns stale pairs. Fix: key cache by all inputs or always recompute from cached membership lookups.

2. [high] clustering_meta is (edge_count, file_count, config_hash), not a membership generation. Membership can change while these values stay identical (e.g. batch_insert_membership doesn't update it). Fix: introduce a real membership generation counter.

Next: fix cache invalidation before wiring into DD enforcement. Add tests with changed constraints, changed path maps, and membership changes with unchanged clustering_meta."
